children: South Korea's economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, as the artificial-intelligence boom continued to drive strong semiconductor exports, offsetting weakness elsewhere.
Gross domestic product expanded 1.0% in July-September from the previous quarter, following 0.6% growth in April-June, preliminary Bank of Korea data showed Tuesday.
The economy grew 3.4% from a year earlier, compared with 3.7% in the second quarter, the data showed.

Third-quarter GDP growth beat market expectations. The median forecast of 19 economists surveyed by The Wall Street Journal was for growth of 0.7% from the previous quarter and 3.3% from a year earlier.

Exports remained a key driver of overall growth, as the global investment in AI infrastructure sustained demand for semiconductors. South Korea is home to memory-chip makers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
Facilities investment, including spending on chip-making equipment and other machinery, increased sharply from the previous quarter, while private consumption contracted.
Construction investment returned to growth in the third quarter, while government spending increased at a faster pace from the previous quarter.
